topics.title: Getting Started
topics.description: What Photoreka is and how the core workflow works

subtopics.title: What is Photoreka?
subtopics.content:
Photoreka is an **intelligent photo curation and organization platform** designed for photographers. It uses artificial intelligence to analyze, classify, score, and help you rediscover photos in your catalog.

The core workflow is:
1. **Upload photos** — Sync Area → Lightbox
2. **Process with AI** — Sync Area → Analysis
3. **Explore and create** — Search, Canvas, Collections, Atlas, and more

The app is available on desktop and mobile, although some tools are desktop-only (Canvas, 3D Atlas, Series).

subtopics.title: Photo Life Cycle
subtopics.content:
Photos move through several internal states as they are processed:

| State | Description |
|---|---|
| **uploaded** | Just uploaded, not analyzed |
| **preprocessing** | Basic pre-analysis in progress |
| **preprocessed** | Ready for full AI analysis |
| **processing** | Full AI analysis in progress |
| **processed** | Fully analyzed and available in all tools |

Photos only appear in Search, Collections, Atlas, Canvas, etc. when they are in the **processed** state. Photos in earlier states are only visible in the Sync Area.

> **Tip:** If photos do not appear in Search or Workspace, they likely haven't been analyzed yet. Go to **Sync Area → Lightbox** and click **Analyze Photos**.

subtopics.title: Dashboard
subtopics.content:
The Dashboard is your home screen after signing in. It acts as a navigation hub and status overview.

**What you'll find:**
- Personalized greeting with your name
- **Daily Eureka Card** — one photo selected from your catalog for rediscovery
- Quick access to main tools: Canvas (with saved canvas preview), Workspace, Report, Atlas
- **Recent Collections & Series** section

**Notes:**
- If you have no processed photos yet, most shortcuts appear locked
- On mobile, desktop-only tools are hidden or replaced (e.g., Explorer instead of Canvas)
- The Daily Eureka Card only appears once you have processed photos

topics.title: Registration & Profile
topics.description: Import mode, photography profile, and how they affect the app

subtopics.title: Choosing Your Import Mode
subtopics.content:
During registration you choose how you prefer to manage photo imports. **This decision is permanent and cannot be changed after setup.**

### Web-first Workflow
Your main import flow is through the Photoreka web interface.
- Upload from your computer (drag & drop or browse)
- Connect Google Photos and sync automatically
- Works from any device with a browser
- Lightroom plugin available as an optional secondary source
- **Best for:** Photographers using multiple sources or preferring web-based management

### Lightroom-first Workflow
Photo imports must **always be done from the Lightroom Plugin** to maintain synchronization.
- Full access to all Photoreka web tools
- Search integrated directly into Lightroom
- **Important:** Uploading photos through the web still works, but those photos won't appear in your Lightroom catalog, causing workflow inconsistencies
- **Best for:** Photographers who organize everything in Lightroom

subtopics.title: Photography Profile
subtopics.content:
During registration you also choose a Photography Profile. **This is also permanent.** It influences how the AI evaluates and organizes your work.

### General Photography
Balanced evaluation across all photographic styles. Ideal for everyday, family, travel, and mixed collections.

### Street Photography
Biased toward candid moments, urban life, human subjects, humor, and visual games in everyday life.

### Documentary Photography
Biased toward narrative strength, emotional impact, authenticity, and photo essay potential.

### Artistic Photography
Biased toward creative vision, conceptual execution, color theory, light, and unique perspectives.

### Dual Profiles
Combination modes are also available:
- **Artistic + Documentary** — Storytelling through artistic expression
- **Artistic + Street** — Creative urban documentation with artistic flair
- **Documentary + Street** — Narrative urban storytelling

subtopics.title: How Your Profile Affects the App
subtopics.content:
Your Photography Profile creates a **slight preference** in how the AI engine evaluates your work:

- **Artistic Scores:** The AI weights qualities relevant to your chosen style when assigning 1–10 scores
- **Search & Recommendations:** Semantic search and Chat recommendations subtly surface photos that align with your declared sensibility
- **Atlas & Visualizations:** The 3D and 2D Atlas prioritize visual and conceptual relationships relevant to your profile

> **Important:** Your profile does **not** restrict uploads. You can upload any type of photo regardless of your chosen profile. The profile only creates a slight preference in how the engine evaluates and organizes your work.

topics.title: Importing Photos
topics.description: Sync Area, Lightbox, and the analysis workflow

subtopics.title: The Sync Area
subtopics.content:
The Sync Area is your entry point for importing and processing photos — the first tool new users should use.

It has two tabs:

### Lightbox Tab
- Lists all photos in **uploaded**, **preprocessing**, or **preprocessed** states
- Upload new photos via drag & drop or file selector
- Connect external sources: **Lightroom Plugin** and **Google Photos**
- Select photos individually or in bulk to send for analysis
- A floating **Analyze Photos** button appears when photos are ready

### Analyses Tab
- Shows photos currently in the **processing** state
- Displays analysis progress
- Allows navigating back to Lightbox

subtopics.title: Uploading Photos
subtopics.content:
Upload photos directly from your computer or mobile device:

1. Go to **Sync Area → Lightbox**
2. Click the upload area or drag and drop files
3. Supported formats: JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC
4. Maximum file size: 20 MB per photo

After upload, photos enter the **preprocessing** stage automatically before becoming ready for full analysis.

subtopics.title: Import from Google Photos
subtopics.content:
Connect your Google Photos account to sync your library:

1. Go to **Settings → Integrations**
2. Click **Connect** next to Google Photos
3. Authorize Photoreka to access your photos
4. Return to **Sync Area → Lightbox** to see synced photos ready for analysis

subtopics.title: Analyzing Photos
subtopics.content:
Once photos are in the Lightbox (preprocessed state), you can send them for AI analysis:

1. Select the photos you want to analyze (or select all)
2. Click the floating **Analyze Photos** button
3. Photos move to the **Analyses** tab while processing
4. When complete, they become **processed** and appear in all tools

> **Tip:** You can analyze photos in batches. You don't need to wait for all photos to finish — tools become available with each photo as it completes.

subtopics.title: Workspace
subtopics.content:
The Workspace (/workspace) is your main library view — a grid of all **processed** photos in your catalog.

**Features:**
- Adjustable grid layout
- Click any photo to open the Photo Info panel
- Multi-select for batch actions (add to collection, send to tool, download)
- Photo counter on mobile

If the Workspace is empty, it will guide you to the Sync Area to upload and analyze photos.

subtopics.title: Collections
subtopics.content:
Collections are **unordered thematic groups** — the equivalent of albums. Ideal for projects, clients, events, or editorial stages.

**To create a collection:**
1. Go to **Collections** in the sidebar
2. Click **New Collection**
3. Give it a name
4. Add photos by dragging, multi-selecting, or using the **Add to Collection** action from Search or Chat

**Managing collections:**
- Rename a collection by clicking its name
- Delete a collection — photos are **not** deleted
- Photos can belong to multiple collections

subtopics.title: Photo Info Panel
subtopics.content:
The Photo Info panel shows a detailed view of any individual photo. Open it by clicking a photo in the Workspace, Search, Canvas, or any other tool.

**Sections:**
- **Metadata** — EXIF data, GPS location, technical specs
- **Tags** — Contextual, Technical, Miscellaneous, and Artistic tags generated by AI
- **Artistic Scores** — AI-assigned ratings on a 1–10 scale across multiple dimensions
- **Genre Presets** — Predefined weight configurations for the global rating
- **Notes** — Personal annotations
- **AI Insights** — Contextual analysis from the AI (limited per session)

The **Global Rating** is a configurable weighted average of the individual artistic scores.

subtopics.title: Semantic Search
subtopics.content:
Write a natural description to find photos by visual and conceptual meaning:

- "market at sunset"
- "child running in the rain"
- "minimalist architecture"
- "portrait with bokeh"

The AI identifies photos matching the meaning of your query. The exact words don't need to appear in any metadata — the engine understands context and visual concepts.

subtopics.title: Tag Search
subtopics.content:
Search by the AI-generated tags assigned to your photos during analysis:

1. Switch to **Tags** mode in the search bar
2. Type a tag name — autocomplete suggests existing tags from your catalog
3. Click tags to **include** them (logical AND)
4. You can also **exclude** specific tags
5. Combine multiple tags for precise filtering

subtopics.title: Search Modes
subtopics.content:
Choose the mode that best fits your query:

### Broad
Light scan across the entire library. Best for **moods**, **compositional aspects**, and **general visual style**. Ideal as a starting point for exploration.

### Adaptive
Context-aware search that enriches your query with related concepts. Best for **metaphors**, **cultural references**, and nuanced conceptual searches.

### Precise
Highly analytical and focused. Best for **specific objects** and **taxonomic distinctions** when you know exactly what you're looking for.

> **Tip:** Start with Broad for exploration. Use Precise when you know exactly what you want. Choose Adaptive for conceptual or metaphorical queries.

subtopics.title: Filters & Results
subtopics.content:
Refine your search results with filters:
- **Visual Aspects** — color, orientation, lighting, depth of field, genre, perspective, and more
- **Artistic Scores** — filter by AI-assigned quality ratings
- **Collections** — search within specific albums

**Result features:**
- Relevance rating (1–3 stars) shown per photo
- High match indicator for strongest results
- Progressive pagination with **Load more**

**Actions from results:**
- Open Photo Info panel
- Multi-select photos
- Add to Collection or Series
- Send to another tool
- Download as ZIP

subtopics.title: 3D Atlas
subtopics.content:
The 3D Atlas is an **immersive three-dimensional visualization** of your catalog based on AI semantic similarity (vector embeddings). Photos that are visually and conceptually similar cluster together. Desktop only.

**Navigation:**
- Orbit, zoom, and pan with mouse or trackpad
- Click any photo to open its info panel

**Features:**
- **Filters** — Visual aspects, artistic scores, time range
- **Inflate factor** — Spread clusters apart for easier exploration
- **Grid relaxation** — Adjust cluster density
- **Floating semantic tags** — Topic labels that emerge from photo clusters
- **Auto tour** — Automated flythrough of your catalog
- **Public shareable URL** — Share your Atlas with anyone

subtopics.title: 2D Atlas
subtopics.content:
The 2D Atlas is a flat semantic map of your catalog — the same AI similarity layout as the 3D Atlas, but as a navigable 2D plane. Mobile compatible.

All the same filters apply: visual aspects, artistic scores, and time range. Use this on mobile or whenever you prefer a flat overhead view of your photo clusters.

subtopics.title: Report & Statistics
subtopics.content:
The Report section provides a **deep analysis of your entire catalog**.

**Sections:**
- **Usage Patterns** — When and how often you photograph
- **Visual Aspects** — Distribution of colors, orientations, lighting styles, genres, and more
- **Artistic Scores Distribution** — Histogram of AI quality ratings across the catalog
- **Portfolio Consistency** — How cohesive your body of work is

Use the Report to understand patterns in your photography and identify strengths or gaps in your catalog.

subtopics.title: Canvas
subtopics.content:
Canvas is an **infinite freeform visual board** for composition, sequencing, and collage. Desktop only.

**Core features:**
- Drag & drop photos onto the board
- Zoom, pan, resize, and rotate freely
- Multi-select and group photos
- Save your board manually (Canvas does **not** auto-save)

**Adding photos:**
1. Open the photos panel within Canvas
2. Drag photos directly onto the board, or use the built-in search to find and add them

subtopics.title: Canvas Expansion
subtopics.content:
Expansion is Canvas's key feature — it automatically **adds related photos** to your board based on similarity.

**Expansion types:**
- **General** — Semantic and compositional similarity
- **Chromatic** — Color palette similarity
- **Narrative** — Contextual and thematic similarity

**Expand from:**
- Your full catalog
- Only the photos already on the canvas

> **Note:** If Canvas shows a "Basic Mode" indicator, it means some photos on the board are unprocessed and full expansion features are limited.

subtopics.title: Series
subtopics.content:
Series are **ordered photo sequences** with narrative intent — designed for photo essays, books, and presentations. Desktop only.

**Features:**
- Drag-and-drop reordering
- Fullscreen slideshow playback
- Public shareable URL for presenting your work

**Collection vs Series:**
- **Collections** are unordered thematic groups
- **Series** are ordered narrative sequences meant for storytelling and presentation

subtopics.title: Framer
subtopics.content:
Framer lets you add **presentation frames** to your photos — perfect for social media posts and print preparation.

**Supported formats:**
- Instagram Posts (1:1, 4:5)
- Instagram Stories (9:16)
- Facebook & Twitter/X Posts
- Print ratios (4:3, 16:9)
- Custom aspect ratios

**Frame settings:**
- **Margin size** — Adjust border width with a slider
- **Frame color** — Choose from presets or a custom color
- **Background** — Solid colors or blur effects
- **Alignment** — Center, top, or bottom positioning

Once configured, preview and download your framed photo.

topics.title: ChatLab
topics.description: ChatLab - Talk to your photos and curate your catalog with our AI assistant

subtopics.title: What the Assistant Does
subtopics.content:
The Photoreka's Assistant (ChatLab) lets you explore and curate your photo catalog through natural conversation. Available on desktop and mobile.

**Key capabilities:**
- Ask questions about your catalog and get contextual insights
- Request curated photo recommendations based on themes, mood, or style
- Explore visual patterns and recurring subjects across your work
- Get analysis of specific photos or collections

The assistant has full knowledge of your processed catalog and uses semantic understanding — not just keyword matching.

subtopics.title: Curating with the Assistant
subtopics.content:
The assistant can surface relevant photos and let you add them directly to Collections or Series — without manual searching.

**Workflow:**
1. Open ChatLab and describe what you're looking for
2. The assistant displays matching photos with an **Add to...** button
3. Click **Add to...** → choose **Collection** or **Series**
4. Select an existing one or create new — photos are added instantly

This lets you build curated groupings conversationally, based on semantic understanding rather than metadata alone.

subtopics.title: Tips for Better Results
subtopics.content:
Get the most out of the AI Assistant:

- **Be descriptive:** "Show me my strongest street photos from the last year" works better than "show photos"
- **Ask for comparisons:** "Which of my photos have the best light?"
- **Request curation:** "Help me build a 10-photo series about urban isolation"
- **Explore themes:** "What subjects appear most often in my catalog?"
- **Combine with tools:** After the assistant surfaces photos, send them directly to Canvas or a Series for further work

> **Note:** The assistant's AI Insights feature on individual photos has a session usage limit.

topics.title: Privacy & Terms
topics.description: Image ownership, AI processing policy, and your data rights

subtopics.title: Image Ownership & Storage
subtopics.content:
Your images are yours:
- You retain **100% ownership and copyright** of all images uploaded
- Photoreka does not sell, license, or redistribute your images without your explicit consent
- Only **reduced, low-resolution versions** are stored on secure servers (Cloudflare R2) for analysis, search, and previews
- **Original high-resolution files are not permanently stored**
- All data is encrypted in transit and at rest

subtopics.title: AI Processing Policy
subtopics.content:
How your images are handled during AI analysis:
- Images are **analyzed only** — they are never edited, transformed, or altered during processing
- Processing uses proprietary open-source AI models and third-party AI services (including Google) under paid/private plans **that do not use images to train their models**
- Images may be temporarily transmitted to providers solely for the requested analysis, under confidentiality agreements — they are **not stored** by these providers

**Consent:** By using Photoreka, you acknowledge and accept that your images will be processed using AI models as described. If you do not agree, refrain from uploading images or using the platform.

subtopics.title: Your Data Rights
subtopics.content:
You are in control of your data:
- **Delete anytime:** You can delete your images at any time
- **Removal timeline:** Upon deletion, stored copies and derived data are removed within 30 days, except where legal retention obligations apply
- **No public sharing:** Images are never shared publicly or with unauthorized third parties
- **Third-party access:** Service providers may access images only as strictly necessary for platform functionality and under binding confidentiality obligations

**Sensitive content disclaimer:** Photoreka is intended for artistic or documentary photographic work suitable for public or professional presentation. The platform is **not recommended** for sensitive, private, or personal images. Users are strongly advised not to upload images containing personal or confidential content.

subtopics.title: Terms of Use
subtopics.content:
Key terms to know:
- You are responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of your account
- You must ensure uploaded content does not infringe third-party rights
- You are responsible for the legality and appropriateness of uploaded content
- Photoreka may suspend accounts violating these terms
- Photoreka provides services "as is" and is not liable for indirect damages arising from use of the platform
- By uploading images, you grant Photoreka a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to store, process, and analyze images solely to provide platform functionalities

subtopics.title: Privacy Policy
subtopics.content:
Our privacy commitments:
- **Minimal data collection** — we only collect what is needed to provide the service
- **No third-party advertising** — your data is never used for ads
- **Right to deletion** — request full removal of your data at any time
- **Transparent practices** — we document how data flows through the platform

For questions about privacy or data handling, contact us at support@photoreka.com.
